items.title: Binance plans staged withdrawal restart on Sunday as FBI investigates
items.why: Update: Binance says it has set aside $6.34 billion to cover the $6.3 billion theft and plans to restart withdrawals in stages on November 1 after security checks. The FBI and Secret Service are investigating; about $3 billion is frozen.
items.action: Assume one compromised device is rarely the whole story: after any incident, check every account and system that device could reach before declaring it contained.

items.title: Attackers are probing a new WordPress core flaw fixed in 7.1.4
items.why: A bug in the WordPress updater can let an outside attacker run code during a core upgrade. Wordfence logged tens of thousands of attempts within a day of the October 28 fix. It affects versions 4.7 through 7.1.3.
items.action: Update WordPress to 7.1.4 (or your branch's patched release) and confirm in the dashboard that the update installed rather than assuming auto-update ran.

items.title: Maximum-severity GitLab flaw is now exploited, CISA warns
items.why: CISA added a GitLab CI/CD flaw patched earlier this month to its exploited list on October 29. It can let an attacker run code on self-managed GitLab servers. Nearly 2,800 instances are exposed online.
items.action: Upgrade self-managed GitLab to 19.4.2, 19.3.5 or 19.2.8 or later, and run GitLab's new threat detections to check for signs of compromise.

items.title: TeamViewer fixes a flaw that lets a hostile host attack the person connecting
items.why: A bug in TeamViewer before 15.83 lets a malicious or compromised computer crash, and on Windows possibly take over, the viewer that connects to it for remote support. No attacks are known yet.
items.action: Update TeamViewer on every support and admin machine, including Portable and Android, to 15.83 or later, and update Host installs too since the same release fixes them.

items.title: Retailer Revolve says hackers took saved customer card numbers
items.why: In an SEC filing, Revolve said attackers used automated means to obtain names, contact details, card numbers and expiry dates saved in customer accounts. Texas filings list about 127,000 affected residents.
items.action: If you store customer cards, move to your payment processor's tokenized storage, and add login protections such as MFA and rate limiting to customer accounts.

items.title: Florida financial aid site breach exposes 4.9 million Social Security numbers
items.why: Florida's Department of Education says names, addresses, birth dates and Social Security numbers of nearly 5 million aid applicants were exposed. The site is offline and the state has not said how attackers got in.
items.action: Warn staff and families who applied for Florida aid to freeze their credit and watch for scam calls or emails that quote their personal details.
